h1: The 8 Best Cordless Chainsaws Under $500 for Serious Property Work, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 cordless chainsaws under $500, with 12 to 20 inch bars from EGO, Greenworks, DEWALT and SEESII, scored on bar and battery.
summary: The EGO POWER+ CS1613 is the best all-round saw at this budget, pairing a 16 inch bar with a 56V 4.0Ah battery. The EGO CS1815 steps up to an 18 inch bar, the EGO CS2000 gives you a 20 inch bar if you already own batteries, and the SEESII 18 inch kit gives you two 5.0Ah packs for the lowest outlay.
intro: A larger bar is the upgrade shoppers reach for first, and it is often the wrong one. A 20 inch bar on a small battery just stalls in the cut, and a saw sold without a battery can cost more than a complete kit once you add a pack and charger. At this budget the real question is whether the whole system, saw plus battery, matches the logs you plan to cut.

That framing shapes this ranking. We reviewed eight saws from their listings: bar length from 12 to 20 inches, platform voltage, battery size, what is included in the box and the tool ecosystem behind each battery. Where a listing leaves out a detail, such as the battery size on one EGO model, we say so.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1613 16 Inch Chain Saw
products.verdict: A 16 inch saw with a 56V 4.0Ah battery and charger, ready to cut out of the box.
products.description:
The CS1613 is a 16 inch cordless saw on EGO's 56V platform, supplied with a 4.0Ah battery and a charger. Working that out, the pack stores around 224 watt-hours.

It wins here because the combination is balanced: a bar long enough for most trees a homeowner takes down, and a battery big enough to finish a log pile without a swap. Nothing else in the group matches that completeness at this price, since several rivals ship with smaller packs or no battery at all.

Buy it if you want one saw for years of property work and plan to share the battery with other EGO tools. The honest limit is cut size, since a 16 inch bar will not fell very large trunks in one pass.
pros: Sixteen inch bar suits most work
products.idealFor: Property owners wanting one dependable saw.
products.skipIf: You regularly cut trunks over 14 inches.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1815 18 Inch Chain Saw
products.verdict: An 18 inch EGO saw sold with a battery, for thicker limbs and larger rounds.
products.description:
The CS1815 is an 18 inch battery chainsaw from EGO, and the listing says it ships with a battery. The listing does not state the pack size, so confirm it on the product page before you buy.

It ranks second because two extra inches of bar cut noticeably thicker wood and make clean work of bigger firewood rounds. It sits behind the CS1613 only because that kit documents its battery, and because a longer bar asks more of the pack on every cut.

Choose it if your regular jobs involve limbs and logs above 14 inches and you can budget for a spare battery. If you mostly handle storm cleanup, the 16 inch kit is easier to swing and just as capable.
pros: Eighteen inch bar cuts thicker wood
products.idealFor: Owners cutting thick limbs and firewood rounds.
products.skipIf: You want the lightest saw to handle.

products.award: Best Bare Tool for EGO Owners
products.name: EGO POWER+ CS2000 20 Inch Chain Saw (Tool Only)
products.verdict: The biggest bar in this group at 20 inches, sold without a battery or charger.
products.description:
The CS2000 is a 20 inch EGO saw sold without the battery and charger, as the listing makes clear. It is a tool-only purchase aimed at people who already own EGO 56V packs.

It ranks third because a 20 inch bar is the longest here and suits larger trees, but the bare-tool format changes the maths. If you do not have a compatible battery and charger, you must buy them separately, and a large saw wants a large pack to avoid bogging down.

Buy it if you own EGO batteries already and need the extra bar length. Skip it if you are starting from nothing, in which case a complete kit costs less overall.
cons: Heavy and long for overhead cuts
products.idealFor: Existing EGO owners cutting larger trees.
products.skipIf: You have no EGO battery yet.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 18 Inch Brushless Chainsaw
products.verdict: An 18 inch brushless saw that shares its 80V battery with more than 75 other tools.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is an 18 inch brushless saw described for felling, limbing, pruning and firewood. It comes with a 2.0Ah battery and rapid charger, and the battery is listed as compatible with more than 75 tools.

It ranks fourth because the platform breadth is its main selling point: one battery can power a mower, a blower and a trimmer too. The 2.0Ah pack, around 160 watt-hours, is the weak link for an 18 inch bar, which is why it sits below the EGO kits.

Buy it if you want to standardize your yard tools on one battery. Pick up a second, larger pack if you plan real cutting sessions.
cons: Needs a spare for big jobs
products.idealFor: Owners standardizing on one yard battery.
products.skipIf: You want long run time from the box.

products.name: SEESII 40V 18 Inch Chainsaw with 2 Batteries
products.verdict: An 18 inch saw with two 5.0Ah batteries, offering the most stored energy per kit.
products.description:
The SEESII 40V 18 inch saw comes with two 5.0Ah batteries. At 40V, each pack stores around 200 watt-hours, so the kit holds roughly 400 watt-hours in total, more than any other bundle here.

It ranks fifth because the energy is excellent but the brand is less proven than EGO, Greenworks and DEWALT. Parts, warranty handling and long-term battery supply matter on a tool you will use for years, and a newer brand gives less certainty on all three.

Choose it if you want the most cutting per dollar and are comfortable with a lesser-known name. Prioritize an established platform if you plan to add other cordless tools.
pros: Two packs double the run time
Eighteen inch bar cuts thicker wood
Most stored energy of any kit
cons: Brand has a shorter track record
products.idealFor: Value buyers who want the longest run time.
products.skipIf: You want a major tool brand.

products.name: DEWALT FLEXVOLT 60V 16 Inch Chainsaw Kit
products.verdict: A 16 inch FLEXVOLT saw and 2Ah battery for people who already use DEWALT gear.
products.description:
The DEWALT FLEXVOLT is a 16 inch saw sold with a 2Ah battery. FLEXVOLT packs are built to move between DEWALT's 20V and 60V tools, which is the real draw.

It ranks sixth because a 2Ah battery limits sustained cutting, and the listing gives no motor or chain details. The ecosystem value is high for someone who owns DEWALT tools, and low for anyone who does not.

Buy it if your battery shelf is already yellow. For a first cordless saw, the EGO kits give more energy and a more complete package.
products.idealFor: People who already own DEWALT batteries.
products.skipIf: This will be your first cordless tool.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1611 16 Inch Chain Saw
products.verdict: The same 16 inch EGO saw with a smaller 2.5Ah battery to cut the cost.
products.description:
The CS1611 is the 16 inch EGO saw with a 56V 2.5Ah battery and charger, storing about 140 watt-hours.

It ranks seventh because, at a $500 budget, the larger 4.0Ah kit is a better use of money for anyone cutting more than occasionally. The smaller pack is still fine for limbs and light firewood, and the saw itself is the same.

Buy it if you want to keep the cost down and plan to buy a second battery later. If you want fewer stops, spend a little more on the CS1613.
pros: Easy to add a bigger pack
products.idealFor: Light users planning to add batteries later.
products.skipIf: You cut firewood in long sessions.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1201 12 Inch Chain Saw
products.verdict: A 12 inch EGO saw with a 2.5Ah battery for trimming and small limbs.
products.description:
The CS1201 is a compact 12 inch chainsaw on the 56V platform, supplied with a 2.5Ah battery and charger.

It ranks last because a 12 inch bar limits cut thickness, and a budget of $500 buys a far more capable saw. Its strength is handling: it is light and quick to position, which makes it the better tool for pruning from a ladder or trimming hedges of woody growth.

Buy it as a second saw for light work, not as your only saw. Pair it with a larger model if you need both.
products.idealFor: A light second saw for pruning.
products.skipIf: It must be your only saw.

methodology.title: System fit, saw plus battery
methodology.description: We judged each saw together with the battery and charger in the box, since a bare tool is not a working kit.

methodology.title: Bar length against battery size
methodology.description: Longer bars were credited only when the pack can feed them, using volts times amp-hours as the energy estimate.

methodology.title: Platform ecosystem
methodology.description: Batteries that run mowers, blowers and other tools earned extra credit for long-term value.

methodology.title: Brand support
methodology.description: Established brands with parts and service networks were scored above newer names with fewer documented details.

methodology.title: Value under $500
methodology.description: Each saw was weighed on what the full kit delivers, not the sticker price of the bare tool.

whatMatters.detail: A long bar pulls more chain through the wood and draws more power. Pairing a 20 inch bar with a small battery leads to bogging and short runs. Match the bar to your thickest regular cut and check the pack's watt-hours, which you get by multiplying volts by amp-hours.

Some listings sell the saw alone, others include a battery and charger, and one kit includes two batteries. A bare tool looks cheap until you add a pack and a charger. Read the in-the-box line closely, especially on EGO models where tool-only versions exist.
A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat and wears more slowly. It helps a small battery last longer on each charge. Look for the term in the listing, because not every model states it.

The battery is the long-term investment, because it powers every other tool you add. EGO 56V, Greenworks 80V, DEWALT FLEXVOLT and SEESII 40V each have a different range of compatible tools. Check which other tools you want before choosing a platform.

A longer bar and a bigger battery make a saw heavier, and fatigue leads to mistakes. A saw you can hold comfortably cuts more safely than a bigger one you struggle with. Check the weight on the listing and consider your strength and the kind of cutting you do.

faq.q: Can I use an EGO battery in the CS2000?
faq.a: Yes, the CS2000 runs on EGO 56V batteries, and it is sold as a tool only. You need to supply the battery and charger, and larger packs suit the 20 inch bar better.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a long-bar saw?
faq.a: Buying a long bar and pairing it with a small battery, then stalling in the cut. Match the pack to the bar and keep the chain sharp.

faq.q: Is a 56V saw worth it over 40V?
faq.a: Voltage alone is not the answer, since watt-hours decide run time. A 40V 5.0Ah pack stores similar energy to a 56V 3.6Ah pack, so compare totals.

faq.q: How do I set up the chain?
faq.a: Mount the bar and chain with the cutters facing forward on top, then tension it so you can lift it slightly off the bar by hand. Fill the oil tank and check tension after the first cuts.

faq.q: How do I look after the battery?
faq.a: Store it indoors, away from heat and freezing temperatures, and avoid leaving it fully drained for months. Charge it partially before long storage.

faq.q: Can I cut frozen or wet wood?
faq.a: Wet wood is fine but dulls the chain faster and slows cuts. Frozen wood is harder on the chain and the battery, so expect shorter run times in cold weather.

finalTake: Buy the EGO POWER+ CS1613 if you want a complete 16 inch kit that handles nearly every homeowner job. Step up to the CS1815 for thicker wood, or the SEESII 18 inch kit if you value two big batteries over brand. Skip the CS2000 unless you already own EGO batteries, and keep the 12 inch saw as a second tool for pruning.
